claims.text: The baseline alloy is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The baseline CoCrFeNiTi alloy is a single-phase, disordered solid solution.
Equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has limited atomic-size mismatch.
The baseline alloy lacks significant short-range order and precipitates.
Limited atomic-size mismatch and the absence of ordering or precipitates produce weak solid-solution strengthening and weak dislocation pinning.
Weak dislocation pinning permits highly mobile dislocation glide in baseline CoCrFeNiTi.
Highly mobile dislocation glide causes favorable ductility and machinability.
Highly mobile dislocation glide causes the baseline alloy to have only moderate hardness and yield strength.
Slight compositional deviations or minor alloying additions can enhance local lattice distortion.
Slight compositional deviations or minor alloying additions can induce short-range ordering or nanoscale precipitation.
Local ordering can create obstacles to dislocation motion.
Enhanced lattice distortion increases dislocation pinning.
Increased dislocation pinning raises hardness and yield strength.
The expected strengthening will be accompanied by a moderate reduction in ductility.
The modified alloy will show a statistically significant increase in yield strength and hardness relative to baseline CoCrFeNiTi under identical testing conditions.
The proposed comparison covers tensile and compression testing from approximately 25 °C to 600 °C using identical strain-rate protocols.
The hypothesis is limited to moderate strain rates and conditions under which no phase transformation occurs.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant hardness and yield-strength increase despite verified enhancement of lattice distortion or ordering would falsify the proposed explanation.

contradictions.description: The intervention permits nanoscale precipitation, while the boundary says the hypothesis applies to single-phase alloys. A precipitate-bearing modified material is not strictly single phase unless the boundary is intended to apply only to the baseline.

The intervention permits adding another minor element, whereas the boundary describes the tested materials as CoCrFeNiTi alloys without clarifying whether a six-element derivative remains within scope.
